I am a 73-year-old man, been farming these three mu for fifty years. My father taught me, and now it is just me since my wife passed and my children work in Shijiazhuang. I only finished primary school, but I know my land. I do not read books about farming—I watch what happens on my own fields and I listen to my neighbors.

This year I will keep the same arrangement as always: two mu for wheat then maize, and one mu for cotton. I thought about planting less cotton because picking gets harder every year with my back, but Lao Zhang down the road said the cotton price was decent last year, and I need the cash. Three mu is not much, but it is what I have.

For the wheat on my two mu, I will plant around October 8th, same time as always. I usually save my own seed, but last year the germination was not so good, so this year I will buy fresh seed from the supply store—about 35 yuan per mu for the common kind, not those fancy expensive varieties. At planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, about 25 kg. Then at Qingming, if the wheat looks a bit yellow, I topdress with half a bag of urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. I do not use more than that—fertilizer is expensive and my land still has some strength. For water, I will irrigate twice: once after planting to help it settle, and once at jointing if the spring is dry. I would like to irrigate a third time at grain filling, but the electricity for the pump costs too much now. I spray herbicide once in the spring. For harvest, I hire the combine—my back cannot handle a sickle anymore. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 10th. The window is tight, only a few days, so I work fast. I buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, same as everyone—40 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow when planting, about 20 kg per mu. Maize does not need as much as wheat. If the summer is dry I might irrigate once at the big trumpet stage, otherwise I skip it. One spray for weeds. For harvest I hire the small maize machine because carrying cobs is too hard for me now. I hope for 420 kg per mu.

The cotton mu is my money crop, but it is hard work at my age. I plant around April 20th with the regular improved seed. Cotton is greedy—I give it 25 kg compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea when it flowers. I need to spray for insects two times, maybe three if the bollworm is bad, plus herbicide once. I irrigate twice, at flowering and when the bolls are growing. Picking is the worst part. I do it myself over three or four picks, slow and steady. Sometimes my nephew comes to help for a day or two, but I do not pay him—he does it for the old man. I hope to get 220 kg per mu of seed cotton.

All together—seed, fertilizer, pesticide, pump electricity, and machine hire—I reckon about 1,100 yuan. That is most of my cash for the year. Every yuan matters when you are alone and the land is small. But I would rather apply a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad year. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps.
